section: Accidental Deaths and Suicides in India 1982
title:
PART-I ACCIDENTAL DEATHS IN INDIA
(ACCIDENTAL DEATHS) Accidental deaths in India, involving national population of over 68 crore people, showed an increase of 3.0 percent during the year 1982, over 1981 while the percentage increase in population figures during 1981 over 1980 was 3.1%. Estimated mid-year population figures for 1982 were not available and in absence of these figures, census figures as on 1-3-1981 have been taken for the calculation of volume of accidental deaths, as well as volume of suicides per lakh of population.
A total of 1,25,993 accidental deaths were recorded by police in the country during 1983 against 1,22,221 accidental deaths recorded in 1981.
Volume of Accidental deaths per lakh of population
A study of the figures from 1975 to 1982 in table-I below revealed that the accidental deaths in India recorded a mixed trend during the period of 8 years from 1975 to 1982 as the total number of accidental deaths 1,13,016 in 1975 came down to 1,11,611 in 1976 and then went up to 1,17,338 in 1977 and 1,18,594 in 1978. This number further came down to 1,08,987 in 1979 but increased continuously up to 1982. From the number 1,16,912 in 1980 it went up to 1,22,221 in 1981 and 1,25,993 in 1982. Thus the number of accidental deaths 1,08,987 was the lowest in 1979. The volume of the accidental deaths per lakh of population also showed the mixed trend and it ranged between 18.8 to 16.7.

Volume of Accidental deaths per lakh of Population in the States, Union Territories and Metropolitan Cities

The All-India volume of accidental deaths per lakh of population went up to 18.42 in 1982 in comparison to 17.87 in 1981. This volume has been calculated on the census figures as on 1-3-1981 during both the years i.e. in 1981 and 1982, in absence of estimated mid-year population figures for 1981 and 1982. For the Union Territories as a whole it was 45.23 in 1982 against 40.72 in 1981 which was more than the all-India average as well as the volume of all the states taken together. The volume of accidental deaths for all the 12 Metropolitan cities taken together (48.53) was also more than the All-India average, states average and the U.Ts. average of (18.42), (18.03) and (45.23) respectively.

The volume of accidental deaths per lakh of population for the states union territories and Metropolitan cities varied from (116.13) for Pune to (3.85) for Kanpur. Although no specific reason could be assigned for the large variation in the volume of accidental deaths in the different states, Union Territories and Metropolitan cities, the difference in topography, density of population, density of traffic and level of industrialisation appear to have contributed to the phenomenon.

Among the states, Maharashtra reported (44.91) the maximum volume of accidental deaths per lakh of population followed by Madhya Pradesh (34.78) Sikkim (33.02), Karnataka (21.51) and Tamil Nadu (21.47).
